report_meta.notes: Kit code, report date (2026-09-24), sex (male) and age (71) all match the spec's worked example for ELVMWB6271 exactly. Client name is printed on the cover page only; per spec it should be stored only in the clients table, not report tables.

headline_metrics.printed_comment: It appears that your microbiome is younger than you! The personalized nutrition plan we've put together for you, will help you keep your microbiome young longer!
Your Wellness Index is high, indicating a low risk of chronic disease. The microbiome profile is not associated with chronic disease-linked microbial patterns.
Poor, With Need For Improvement: Although you have a pretty low level of diversity, our personalized nutrition plan will help you improve it and achieve a more diverse microbiome.

Your F/B ratio is high. This means Firmicutes are more dominant, which may be linked to increased calorie extraction and a greater tendency toward weight gain in some people. With your personalized nutrition guide, it's possible to modulate your microbiome!

gut_scores.notes: Spec's own metric_markers example row ('bowel_mobility, Increased intestinal motility, 69') matches this bar; used to calibrate which of the two close low-end numbers (29/35) is the community value vs the labeled marker across all gut-score bars with a close pair.

gut_scores_markers_reading_note: On several gut-score bars, two close numbers are printed near one end (e.g. '29 35' for bowel mobility). The spec's own metric_results example ('bowel_mobility, 69, community 35') confirms the HIGHER of the close pair is the community value and the LOWER is the printed/labeled reference marker; this convention was applied consistently to processed_food_index, antibiotic_damage, autoimmune_index and sleep_quality. Precision on this specific point could not be double-checked against pixel-level bar positions, only against the one example the spec itself gives, so treat community_value on those five scores as the best available reading rather than certain.

krona_abundance_reading_note: Krona chart is a small multi-ring radial chart with curved, overlapping label text; percentages for the named outer-ring slices above are read with reasonably high confidence, but root/phylum/order level ring segments (Bacteria, Firmicutes, Clostridiales, Bacteroidetes, Actinobacteria) did not have individually legible percentages in the rendered image. The visible named slices sum to ~80%, consistent with an additional ~20% in the unlabeled '5 more' wedge and the unread inner rings.

risk_analysis_conditions.notes: The Risk Analysis summary table's 'not at risk' calls for TMA Conversion and Propionate Biosynthesis appear to conflict with the detailed pathway tables later in the report, which show several bacteria as High/Low for those same pathways (e.g. Bacillus, Clostridium, Eubacterium High in TMA; Prevotella copri, Dialister, Akkermansia muciniphila Low and Bacteroides uniformis, Coprococcus catus, Roseburia High in Propionate). This is an additional inconsistency beyond the two the spec explicitly flags, observed while extracting this report; see data_quality_issues_observed in the top-level notes.

ulcerative_colitis.notes: Known catalogue conflict: Dorea is positively associated with Ulcerative Colitis here but negatively associated with Crohn's Disease above (both status High) — stored as printed per spec.

butyric_acid_biosynthesis.notes: Table lists butyrate producers without explicit Positively/Negatively Associated split; all are producers of butyric acid (beneficial / anti-inflammatory role).

propionate_biosynthesis.notes: Known status conflict: Prevotella copri is Low here but Not Detected in the Potential Autoimmune Triggers safety panel (page 11). See data_quality_conflicts.

tma_conversion.notes: Known status conflict: Bacillus is High here but Not Detected in the Dysbiotic/Overgrowth Bacteria safety panel (page 11). See data_quality_conflicts. All 28 rows printed under a single 'Positively Associated' heading, spanning PDF pages 30-31 (footer pages 30-31).

anti_inflammatory_activity_intro.notes: Page 28 is explanatory text only (Butyric Acid / Polyamine / Propionate Biosynthesis definitions); the actual per-bacterium table for these three pathways is on page 29 and is captured above as separate entries.

data_quality_conflicts_expected.detail: Bacillus: Not Detected in Dysbiotic/Overgrowth Bacteria safety panel (page 11) vs High in TMA Conversion pathway table (page 30).
Prevotella copri: Not Detected in Potential Autoimmune Triggers safety panel (page 11) vs Low in Propionate Biosynthesis pathway table (page 29).
Dorea listed as positively associated with Ulcerative Colitis (High, page 24) but negatively associated with Crohn's Disease (High, page 23).
Campylobacter coli appears twice in the Pathogenic Bacteria panel (page 10), rows 3 and 14, both Not Detected.

Curcumin scored 9 (page 35, Phytochemicals); N-3 Fatty Acids scored 1 (page 40, Lipids); Fructooligosaccharide (FOS) scored 2 (page 39, Carbohydrates). The matching food-side scores (turmeric 4, salmon 2/fish oil supplement 8, garlic and onion 6) live in the user report, not this doctor report.
Wellness Index is 'Good' (page 3) while Diversity is 0.5, an 'act' band value (page 4).

The references list may continue beyond page 48 on a page not captured in the page ranges read, or the PDF's reference list may simply stop at 70 while later citation numbers in the pathway tables were not all given a matching list entry. This is a gap to verify against the source PDF directly (re-check pages 46-49 at higher resolution, or confirm whether references 71-91 exist elsewhere in the document). No DOI URLs were printed anywhere in the references section; all entries are citation text only.
